decisions.mark: explains that the health monitor does NOT invoke its status callback from the monitor thread — it queues events under a mutex and the caller drains them on its own thread
decisions.detail: QUOTE: The health monitor never runs user code on its own thread. `monitor_loop` pushes events onto `event_queue_`, and `process_events()` swaps the queue out under `event_mutex_` and invokes the callbacks on the engine thread after releasing the lock (`health_monitor.cpp:118`). | WHY: The answer states that the monitor queues events under a mutex and callbacks are invoked by the drainer on the engine thread, not the monitor thread. || QUOTE: The health monitor never runs user code on its own thread. `monitor_loop` pushes events onto `event_queue_`, and `process_events()` swaps the queue out under `event_mutex_` and invokes the callbacks on the engine thread after releasing the lock (`health_monitor.cpp:118`). | WHY: The answer states that the monitor queues events under a mutex and the callbacks are invoked by the draining caller on the engine thread, not the monitor thread. || QUOTE: The health monitor never runs user code on its own thread. `monitor_loop` pushes events onto `event_queue_`, and `process_events()` swaps the queue out under `event_mutex_` and invokes the callbacks on the engine thread after releasing the lock (`health_monitor.cpp:118`). | WHY: The answer states the monitor queues events under a mutex and the caller drains them and invokes callbacks on its own (engine) thread, not the monitor thread.

decisions.mark: identifies the cancellation observer thread as existing to bridge an atomic into a plain int, because the C ABI boundary cannot carry an atomic
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "The C ABI only ever sees `int*`, so no `std::atomic` crosses the `.so` boundary." and "Interrupt observer | `response_generator.cpp:413` | Mirrors the engine's interrupt flag into an `int` for the duration of one batch call" | WHY: The answer says the observer mirrors an atomic interrupt flag into a plain int, and it says the C ABI only sees `int*`, so no atomic crosses the boundary. That covers the bridging purpose. || QUOTE: "The pollers and observers read a flag every 10 ms and set an atomic. ... The C ABI only ever sees `int*`, so no `std::atomic` crosses the `.so` boundary." and "Interrupt observer ... Mirrors the engine's interrupt flag into an `int` for the duration of one batch call" | WHY: The answer says the observer/poller threads bridge an atomic flag to a plain `int*` because the C ABI can't carry `std::atomic`.
